text:
eva: Quick question — we're planning to tweak per-route burst behavior for /v1/generate (lower burst tokens from 2000 -> 1000) and also change the 429 header semantics. Wanted to surface compatibility concerns before the rollout.

sam: What's the header change?

eva: Right now we set X-RateLimit-Reset as seconds-until-reset (int). New proposal: return unix epoch (seconds). The SDKs in a few customers (and our examples) assume delta semantics.

maria: That will break client-side backoff math unless we bump a major version. Can we keep both types for a transitional period? eg include X-RateLimit-Reset-TS (epoch) + X-RateLimit-Reset (delta) for 2 weeks? :thinking:

eva: I proposed returning both for 14 days and adding a deprecation header X-RateLimit-Deprecated: reset-delta to signal intent. Thoughts on header naming?

own: We should avoid proliferating similar headers. Alternative: keep X-RateLimit-Reset as delta but add X-RateLimit-Reset-TS. That keeps existing clients safe and gives a clear new field.

sam: Agreed. Also need to confirm behavior for per-route vs global quotas. When /v1/generate hits per-route burst, do we 429 immediately or try fallback to a lower-capacity model variant?

eva: Plan is: primary route 429s when the route's token budget is exhausted. Smart routing could transparently route to a cheaper compatible model only for Hosted tier, not Dedicated (customer-configured). The API contract should document that fallback is not guaranteed and clients must handle 429.

maria: Can we add an optional Retry-After seconds header on 429 and keep X-RateLimit-Reset-TS for the canonical time? Some clients trust Retry-After more.

own: We already include Retry-After in a few error paths. For fairness, let's ensure Retry-After is always present on 429 with an integer seconds value. Also add X-RateLimit-Remaining-Tokens and X-RateLimit-Limit-Tokens per-route so clients can tune pacing.

sam: Example 429 response I'd expect: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-RateLimit-Limit-Tokens: 10000
X-RateLimit-Remaining-Tokens: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 12            # delta (backcompat)
X-RateLimit-Reset-TS: 1770004932  # epoch
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "rate_limited", "detail": "route burst exhausted" }
```

eva: That looks good. A couple of nuance items: 1) For streaming token-based responses, we might stream a 429 mid-stream — do we send headers then, or a final error frame?

own: For SSE/stream we emit a terminal event with the error payload and include the same header set in the final HTTP response metadata (and include minimal fields in the event body). Docs should call out that streaming clients need to handle mid-stream termination.

maria: Backward compatibility checklist:
- keep X-RateLimit-Reset as delta for 30 days (not 14) to give customers time
- add X-RateLimit-Reset-TS immediately
- document Retry-After as canonical for naive clients but recommend X-RateLimit-Reset-TS for absolute timing
- surface per-route IDs: X-RateLimit-Route: generate.v1 so client can correlate

eva: Sounds reasonable. Sam — can you add a unit/integration test that verifies both headers present and SDK parsing continues to work? Also add a compatibility note in the API contract doc.

sam: Yep. I'll add tests to rate-limiter unit suite and a small e2e that simulates a legacy client parsing delta. Will post PR today.

own: Ops note — when we flip the default burst limit, we'll run a canary for 6 hours in us-west and watch 429 spike. rate-limiter-bot will auto-roll back if 5xx/429 > 3x baseline.

rate-limiter-bot: Canary started on eng-defaults pool (us-west) — monitoring for error-rate > 3x baseline.

maria: One more API contract detail — need to define semantics for quotas vs instantaneous bursts. Add a small diagram and table saying: 'burst: temporary allowance for short spikes; quota: sustained token window per minute/hour'.

eva: Agreed. I'll update the open PR for api-contract/rate-limits.md with the table + example responses and ping @sam for the tests. Plan: ship headers change + per-route burst reduction next Thursday during low-traffic window.

sam: PR: https://git.redwood.ai/rate-limiter/pulls/174 — adding tests and header docs, will request review. :thumbsup:

own: Leave a note in runbook for SDK teams to watch and communicate with top customers.

maria: LGTM, thanks.

eva: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the doc diff and release checklist.
